title: Favorite pianist, saxophonist and clarinetists
summary: He preferred Georgie Parker on piano, Paul Barnes on sax, and played with George Lewis and Big Eye Lewis.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Are there any other musicians that you can remember now you like that you worked with that were good, like you talked about Piku and helping with those arrangements and helping the rest of the band?

Yeah. I was a piano player. I'll tell you about piano player who I'd rather work with than any of them. That was Georgie Parker. Yeah. I played with plenty of good ones, but I'd rather work with him than any of them. Because he worked with a drummer all the time. You know why?
He had a good left hand. He'd keep the right leg in condition. That's right. He'd play some piano. That's right. Watch his left hand and never would go wrong.
Yeah, he'd play some piano. He's a good piano player.
Yeah, he'd hit chords on the beat and so on.

A saxophone player, I mean, when I first started I'd rather work with Paul Bones than any of them. That's what I'm telling you, at his time, I mean. At his time, I mean, I'd rather work with him in a good piano. He'd play some ball in his time. Yeah, he was a good saxophone player, I mean. If that I'd point out to you, he was alright, but I'd rather Paul style.
Are there any other clarinet players you liked besides Piku?

Well, George Lewis worked with me a good while. Before he had a band, George Lewis worked with me. How about Big Eye Lewis? Big Eye Lewis, I played with him a while. He worked with me a while. Because see, them fellas never had any work, now he should allow all of them a chance.
